title: The King of Glory Sends His Son
description: The King of Glory Sends His Son in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 136, headed “Miracles at the birth of Christ”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The King of Glo-ry sends his Son To make his en-trance on this earth! Be-hold the mid-night bright as noon, And heav-enly hosts de-clare his birth!

lines: The King of Glory sends his Son
To make his entrance on this earth!
Behold the midnight bright as noon,
And heavenly hosts declare his birth!
What wonders and what glories meet!
An unknown star arose, and led
The eastern sages to his feet.
Inward they felt the sacred fire,
And bless'd the babe, and own'd his Name.
Let Jews and Greeks blaspheme aloud,
And treat the holy Child with scorn;
Our souls adore th' eternal God

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
